material_preparation: Fresh A. annua herb was soaked 2 or 12 h and wrung, or pounded and squeezed; dried-herb infusion was the comparator.
chemistry_measurement: Artemisinin quantified by gas-liquid chromatography; pounded juice 293 mg/L, 12-h wrung juice 72.6 mg/L, 2-h wrung juice 45.9 mg/L, dried-herb infusion 14.5 mg/L in the selected high-artemisinin material.
parasite_model: P. falciparum NF54 in vitro; P. berghei-infected mice for oral preparations.
primary_outcome: Pounded juice showed the highest in-vitro activity and only pounded juice suppressed mouse parasitemia; reported suppression reached 52%, 95%, and 96% with one, two, and three 9 mg/kg artemisinin-equivalent doses at 12-h intervals.
host_control_or_selectivity: Preparation comparison and infected-mouse control were reported; no human efficacy or standardized-product control.
constituent_attribution: Artemisinin exposure explains much of the preparation effect, but juice IC50 values were lower than expected from artemisinin alone; co-metabolite contribution remains a hypothesis.
remaining_eligibility_gate: Extract total-dose and clinical-equivalence checks remain open; do not treat fresh juice as an interchangeable clinical formulation.

material_preparation: Water infusions of early-flowering leaves from Cameroon and Luxembourg plants, collected in different years and classified as artemisinin-type versus arteannuin-B-type.
chemistry_measurement: Preparative HPLC/PDA profiles and beta-haematin biomineralization; a 10% Cameroon infusion had A405 0.075 versus 1.515 for Luxembourg, and the Cameroon material was reported elsewhere in the article to contain about 1.2% artemisinin versus four-fold less in Luxembourg.
parasite_model: In-vitro ferriprotoporphyrin IX/beta-haematin surrogate; no direct parasite culture endpoint.
primary_outcome: Cameroon infusion inhibited beta-haematin formation more strongly across tested dilutions and showed more major chromatographic features than Luxembourg infusion.
host_control_or_selectivity: Sixteen individual experiments were reported for the surrogate assay; this is not a host-selectivity experiment.
constituent_attribution: Origin-, chemotype-, and matrix-level association; no terpene-specific attribution and no direct parasite target.
remaining_eligibility_gate: Surrogate endpoint and incomplete matched cultivation metadata preclude direct antimalarial efficacy or terpene-specific inclusion.

material_preparation: Dried leaves from voucher-authenticated A. annua SAM cultivar and A. afra SEN were extracted separately with dichloromethane, methanol, or hot water; extracts were normalized by artemisinin content for several assays.
chemistry_measurement: A. annua SAM leaves contained 15.9 mg/g dry-weight artemisinin and 2.8 mg/g total flavonoids; A. afra SEN contained 0.037 mg/g artemisinin and 2.03 mg/g total flavonoids. GC-MS quantified artemisinin and an aluminum-chloride assay estimated total flavonoids.
parasite_model: P. falciparum 3D7, MRA1252/MRA1240, and K13 R539T Cam3.II/Cam3.IIrev strains; 72-h growth assays, 6/8/24-h ring-stage survival assays, and pooled human-serum experiments.
primary_outcome: DLA extracts showed strain- and exposure-time-dependent activity; the resistant Cam3.IIrev comparison converged with longer exposure, and pooled malaria-exposed sera inhibited parasite growth by at least 70% in the reported serum experiments.
host_control_or_selectivity: Pure artemisinin, DHA, CoArtem, resistant/sensitive strains, solvent controls, and malaria-naive versus malaria-exposed pooled sera were used; host interaction was proposed, not proven.
constituent_attribution: Artemisinin content tracks much of the activity, while extract/serum effects support candidate matrix or host interactions; no specific non-artemisinin terpene was isolated as causal.
remaining_eligibility_gate: Full dose-response extraction and independent reanalysis of strain-normalized endpoints remain required before quantitative synthesis.

material_preparation: Whole-plant water infusions of A. annua and A. afra were compared, with concentrations reported as dry leaf mass per litre.
chemistry_measurement: The study contrasted an artemisinin-containing A. annua infusion with artemisinin-free A. afra; active non-artemisinin chemistry was not resolved to individual terpenes.
parasite_model: P. falciparum blood stages; P. berghei and P. falciparum hepatic stages; P. vivax and P. cynomolgi schizonts and hypnozoites in primary hepatocytes.
primary_outcome: Both infusions inhibited blood and liver stages at low leaf-equivalent concentrations; 10 g/L A. annua and 4 g/L A. afra cleared the reported P. falciparum hepatic cultures, and hypnozoite disruption was observed in the relapsing-species experiments.
host_control_or_selectivity: Primary simian and human hepatocyte toxicity observations, vehicle/drug comparators, stage comparisons, and organelle imaging were reported.
constituent_attribution: The authors interpreted the shared effects as essentially artemisinin-independent, but the active compounds and direct targets were not identified; the result is infusion-level evidence.
remaining_eligibility_gate: Quantitative stage-specific dose extraction, chemical profiling, and replication with defined fractions remain open.

material_preparation: Twenty-four experimentally infected lambs received unsupplemented feed, dried A. absinthium stem at 1 g dry matter/day, dried mallow, or the plant mix for 75 days; matched aqueous extracts were tested in an egg-hatch assay.
chemistry_measurement: UHRMS/HR-Q-TOF-MS characterized phenolic fractions; A. absinthium contained detected terpenoids but the reported quantitative chemistry emphasized phenolic acids and flavonoids, including 0.35 g/kg dry matter total flavonoids.
parasite_model: H. contortus eggs in vitro and experimentally infected lambs with serial fecal egg counts and terminal worm counts.
primary_outcome: A. absinthium aqueous extract ED50 and ED99 were 1.40 and 3.76 mg/mL in vitro; mean fecal egg counts and terminal worm counts did not differ significantly among treated and untreated lamb groups.
host_control_or_selectivity: Four six-lamb groups, untreated controls, mixed-plant comparator, serial EPG, and necropsy endpoints were reported; no terpene-specific host safety or exposure estimate.
constituent_attribution: Strong ovicidal activity did not translate to a significant in-vivo group effect; the authors discuss bioavailability, rumen metabolism, and mixture synergy rather than a terpene mechanism.
remaining_eligibility_gate: Dose normalization to constituent exposure, individual-animal variability, and full constituent-level attribution remain open.

material_preparation: Air-dried A. absinthium leaves were rinsed briefly with dichloromethane; the crude rinse was fractionated and artemetin plus hydroxypelenolide were isolated.
chemistry_measurement: Vouchered material and dichloromethane leaf-rinse extraction; isolated compounds were identified by NMR and tested at 100 micromolar.
parasite_model: Adult S. mansoni pairs from the BH strain, maintained in hamsters and tested for 48 h in vitro.
primary_outcome: A. absinthium crude extract caused 100% mortality at 200 microgram/mL and all pairs were dead at 50 and 100 microgram/mL after 48 h; artemetin and hydroxypelenolide were inactive at 100 micromolar.
host_control_or_selectivity: RPMI and 0.5% DMSO negative controls plus 5 micromolar praziquantel positive control; mammalian-cell selectivity was not established for the A. absinthium crude extract.
constituent_attribution: The fractionation narrowed the A. absinthium signal to a preparation-level activity, but the two isolated constituents tested were inactive; this is not evidence that either is the active wormwood molecule.
remaining_eligibility_gate: Dose-response extraction, active-fraction identity, host-cell selectivity, and in-vivo confirmation remain open.

material_preparation: Fresh A. annua leaves were steam-distilled for 4 h; oil yield was 0.6% on a dry-weight basis and the oil was diluted in DMSO for assays.
chemistry_measurement: GC-MS identified camphor 52.06%, beta-caryophyllene 10.95%, 1,8-cineole 5.57%, beta-caryophyllene oxide 4.21%, and beta-farnesene 3.83% among the reported constituents.
parasite_model: L. donovani promastigotes, intracellular amastigotes in RAW 264.7 macrophages, and infected BALB/c mice.
primary_outcome: IC50 was 14.63 plus or minus 1.49 microgram/mL for promastigotes and 7.3 plus or minus 1.85 microgram/mL for intracellular amastigotes; 50/100/200 mg/kg/day for 10 days reduced liver burden by 45.26/63.23/88.68% and spleen burden by 72.48/80.72/91.66%.
host_control_or_selectivity: No macrophage cytotoxicity was observed up to 200 microgram/mL in the reported assay; organ enzymes remained in the reported normal range in treated mice; amphotericin B and untreated/vehicle controls were included.
constituent_attribution: The phenotype is for a camphor-rich whole oil; apoptosis, ROS, mitochondrial, and nitric-oxide changes are oil-level mechanistic correlates, not proof that camphor or beta-caryophyllene alone is causal.
remaining_eligibility_gate: Defined-component testing, formulation exposure, broader host safety, and independent in-vivo replication remain open.

material_preparation: Aerial A. absinthium material was macerated 72 h in 70% ethanol, turbo-extracted, filtered, and tested as a 10% stock with five serial dilutions; LC/MS profiled the alcoholic extracts.
chemistry_measurement: LC/MS detected polyphenols, tocopherols, sterols, methoxylated flavones, and sesquiterpene lactones in the A. absinthium extract; individual terpene concentrations were not established in the parasite assay.
parasite_model: Non-embryonated A. suum eggs and L1/L2-L3 development in a 21-day in-vitro assay, with five replicates and 100 eggs per dilution.
primary_outcome: All tested plant extracts inhibited some developmental endpoints in a concentration-dependent manner; A. absinthium was among the stronger extracts, but the article reports a mixed-extract effect rather than a terpene-specific potency.
host_control_or_selectivity: 70% ethanol and distilled-water controls plus five other botanical extracts; no mammalian-cell or in-vivo host selectivity endpoint in this experiment.
constituent_attribution: Sesquiterpene lactones were detected as part of a chemically complex extract, but the study did not identify the active molecule or protein target.
remaining_eligibility_gate: Exact row-level concentration-response values and constituent-normalized comparison remain open; retain as crude-extract evidence.

material_preparation: Aerial parts from ten Benin plantations and one French location were vouchered, dried at 45 degrees C for one week, ground, and prepared as 1 g in 200 mL boiling water for 15 min; a one-year storage comparison was included.
chemistry_measurement: Artemisinin was quantified by LC-MS/MRM and untargeted LC-HRMS metabolomics was used for tea profiles; artemisinin ranged from 0.3 mg/L in French tea to 15.7 mg/L in the highest Benin tea, while storage losses at three Benin localities were 33%, 48%, and 24%.
parasite_model: Chloroquine-sensitive P. falciparum 3D7 in a 42-h tritiated-hypoxanthine incorporation assay with triplicate independent plates.
primary_outcome: Artemisinin concentration and tea antiplasmodial activity were positively correlated; the artemisinin-equivalent IC50 comparison suggested enhancing or limiting co-metabolites, and unknown alkaloids correlated with activity.
host_control_or_selectivity: Matched pure-artemisinin comparison, triplicate parasite assays, vouchered plantation sampling, and storage comparisons were reported; no clinical or host-selectivity endpoint.
constituent_attribution: This is origin-, storage-, and matrix-level evidence. Candidate co-metabolites were statistically associated but not purified or proven to be terpenes or causal effectors.
remaining_eligibility_gate: Full metabolite identities, raw concentration-response extraction, and constituent-level validation remain open; do not equate tea activity with standardized artemisinin treatment.
